statement: For Theorem 1 Algorithm 3 memories and a query within r=1/sqrt(beta N) of a stored pattern, Theorem 3 bounds one-step retrieval error by 3/sqrt(beta N); substituting N=Omega(exp(d alpha^2/16)) makes the error exponentially small in dimension.
acceptance: A proof certificate derives the dimension exponent -alpha^2/32 from the exact theorem size.
Every query satisfies W2(query,target)<r and all commuting/spectral assumptions.
Every log-domain one-step error certificate is below 3/sqrt(beta N).
The upper 95% confidence bound on observed log-error slope is at most -alpha^2/32.
A long-double direct checker is bounded by the independent log-domain certificate.
A sign-reversed Gibbs-weight control violates the theorem bound.
